entries.title: iReader Air 3 Pro E-Reader is coming out soon
entries.summary: The iReader Air 3 Pro is an 8.2-inch e-reader and e-note device that stands out in the e-paper market due to its unique screen size and specific design choices intended to maximize text clarity. The post iReader Air 3 Pro E-Reader is coming out soon first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The iReader Air 3 Pro is an 8.2-inch e-reader and e-note device from PalmRead. It stands out in the e-paper market due to its unique screen size and specific design choices intended to maximize text clarity. It is launching in China on August 6, 2026, and no pricing is available yet.

It features an 8.2-inch E Ink Carta 1300 screen with a resolution of 300 PPU and 00 PPI class, and up to a 50 fps refresh rate. The e-reader offers responsive e-paper generation with significantly darker blacks and higher contrast. In an unconventional hardware shift, iReader omitted the traditional built-in frontlight from this model. By removing the light guide layer, the e-paper screen is essentially transparent, reducing the gap between your eyes and the electronic ink. This delivers an ultra-sharp, paper-like reading experience but requires external ambient light to read in dark environments.

The device integrates physical page-turn buttons along the side bezel, making it highly ergonomic for single-handed reading. It includes an electromagnetic stylus for sketching, note-taking, and direct annotation of PDFs or e-books. The device includes expandable storage capabilities, giving it an edge over competing devices with locked internal storage capacities.

Under the hood is an 8-core CPU and a dedicated microSD slot supporting external storage up to 2TB. Runs Android-based SmartOS, though iReader’s stock interface is tailored primarily for the Chinese domestic market and does not have Google Play, but users will be able to install their own apps.

Michael Kozlowski has written about audiobooks, e-books and e-readers for the past eighteen years. He Lives in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

entries.title: Pocketbook Era Lite E-reader Review
entries.summary: The Pocketbook Era Lite is a budget-friendly 7-inch e-reader featuring a sharp E Ink Carta 1300 screen, physical page-turn buttons, and an open format ecosystem, offering the core reading experience of the standard Pocketbook Era at a lower price point by omitting a built-in speaker. The post Pocketbook Era Lite E-reader Review first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The PocketBook Era Lite is a 7-inch black-and-white e-reader released in mid-2026 as a budget-friendly, reading-focused alternative to the premium standard PocketBook Era. It serves as a direct competitor to Amazon’s Kindle Paperwhite. It distinguishes itself by offering an open ecosystem, native library borrowing, and tactile hardware buttons.

Hardware

The Pocketbook Era Lite features a 7-inch E INK Carta 1300 e-paper display with a resolution of 1264×1680 and 300 PPI. The device is black and has physical page-turn buttons on the right side, similar to those on the previous-generation Pocketbook Era and Pocketbook Era Color. The PocketBook Era Lite features an asymmetrical, ergonomic design optimized for comfortable, one-handed reading. By removing the extra layer of protective cover glass, the device minimizes screen reflections and improves text contrast. The absence of a flush screen and bezel contributes to amazing contrast.

Unlike the flush glass front of the original Era, the Era Lite utilizes a recessed display with a raised bezel. The build is similar to the Era but has a sunken screen and bezel. By removing the extra layer of protective cover glass, the device minimizes screen reflections and improves text contrast. The absence of a flush screen and bezel contributes to amazing contrast.

Era Lite features IPX4-rated water resistance, designed to protect the device from splashes and moisture in everyday use. You don’t need to worry about using it with wet hands or if a few drops of water land on it while you’re relaxing by the pool. The e-reader also features adaptive SMARTlight technology that adjusts both brightness and color temperature to suit different environments. Because the light is distributed across the screen rather than shining directly into users’ eyes, it feels softer and less intrusive than on standard displays. Warm tones support nighttime reading, while cooler tones suit daytime reading perfectly.

Under the hood is a dual-core 1 GHZ processor, 1GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage to house all your e-books purchased from the Pocketbook Store or sideloaded. The e-reader also supports audiobooks via Bluetooth 5.1; Era Lite lets users listen to their favourite titles anytime. Its Text-to-Speech feature allows the device to read aloud any text file in a range of languages, using clear, natural voices. Users can start reading and switch to listening with just a few taps, with the e-reader resuming at the exact page. This makes it easy to switch between formats depending on the situation – from focused reading to moments when listening is more convenient, such as driving, cooking, or multitasking. It transforms the Era Lite into a versatile everyday companion. It is powered by a 1700 mAh battery.

Software

Pocketbook has always run Linux on all of its e-readers. This is the same operating system used by the Amazon Kindle and Kobo e-readers. This OS helps preserve battery life because no background processes are being run. It is also rock-stable and seldom crashes. It is super stable, although this prevents users from installing any apps on the device.

If you tap the top of the screen, you’ll see a number of quick-action settings. This is similar to Android when you tap or swipe down from the top. You can adjust the brightness of the front-lit display and color temperature settings. Establish a Wi-Fi network, pair Bluetooth headphones, enable system-wide dark mode, or activate airplane mode.

The main home screen features a widget at the top that showcases the books you are reading or have downloaded from the store but haven’t started yet. If there are a few books you are in the process of reading, there is a multi-page layout you can swipe through to see the next few books on the carousel. Underneath that are some recommended books from the Pocketbook Store; you will see around nine bestselling titles. The main navigation features icons with text, and there are three pages you can swipe through.

Your library is where all of your content is housed, and you can filter it by format, author, or date, and sort it in list view or cover art view. If some of your books still need to have cover art images because you downloaded them online, a metadata system will look at the book’s title and author and fetch metadata for it. You will likely be on this screen because you buy and load hundreds of books. You can also hit switches on a particular book to flag it as finished, making it disappear from the home screen.

Audiobooks is another home screen UI element where you can load your own audiobooks or download them from the Pocketbook Store. There is an audiobook folder in the settings menu that lets you establish where you want to store your audiobook content. The main player officially supports M4A, M4B, OGG, OGG.ZIP, MP3, and MP3.ZIP.

The Store is the next feature, and our review unit was locked to the UK bookstore, which has 4.5 million e-books and 90,000 audiobooks – including international bestsellers and beloved classics – with easy access to and purchase of any eBook from the catalog directly on the e-reader. All purchases will be stored not only on the Pocketbook InkPad One but also on all other Pocketbook e-readers and their apps.

If you want to download books for free, the Pocketbook Era Lite supports Libby out of the box.PocketBook users will now be able to log in with their library card, borrow titles through the PocketBook x Libby app, and seamlessly read or listen on their e-reader. Titles can also be sampled before borrowing. Ebooks can be downloaded for offline reading within the borrowing period. Other formats, including audiobooks, are streamed or accessed through the browser. You need a digital library card, your branch, and a 4-digit PIN code. Reading

This e-reader is designed for reading books, and users can access the Pocketbook Store to download thousands of books. However, the real power lies in sideloading your content, which supports DRM EPUB and PDF files, as well as books downloaded online. It offers extensive support for ACSM, AZW, AZW3, CBR, CBZ, CHM, DJVU, DOC, DOCX, EPUB (DRM), EPUB, FB2, FB2.ZIP, HTM, HTML, MOBI, PDF (DRM), PDF, PRC, RTF, and TXT. With DRM EPUB and PDF, users can purchase ebooks from other stores such as Barnes & Noble, Kobo, and Google.

You can use Libby natively on the Era Lite via the built-in PocketBook x Libby app. Introduced in late 2025 via firmware version 6.10 or higher, this official integration allows you to browse, borrow, and read library titles directly on your e-reader without using a computer web browser or transferring files over Adobe Digital Editions. Ebooks can be downloaded for offline reading within the borrowing period.”, according to OverDrive. Downloaded files automatically load inside the native PocketBook Reading app. Borrowed titles return automatically when the loan period expires, but you can choose to return them early directly from your device desktop or the app’s “Manage Loan” interface

Users can also enjoy the convenience of 11 preloaded dictionaries and explore an additional 42 language combinations, available for free download. Whether learning a new language or enhancing your language skills, PocketBook Verse Lite is the perfect companion for language enthusiasts.

Last year, PocketBook launched a UK bookstore, and most of its new e-readers have the store built in, no matter what country they live in. It offers 4.5 million e-books and 90,000 audiobooks that cover every genre. Readers gain access not only to timeless favourites but also to international premieres – with many of the world’s top bestsellers available on the same day as their global release. Regular updates, diverse genres, and works from renowned authors ensure the store remains dynamic, relevant, and full of discoveries.

With a pay-per-download model, UK readers now have direct access to millions of e-books and audiobooks. This expansion highlights PocketBook’s commitment to delivering the most advanced and user-friendly reading experiences worldwide.

“We’re proud to open this new PocketBook chapter in the UK. By adding Gardner’s rich catalog to our ecosystem, we’re making e-reading even more accessible to users across the UK,” said Enrico Mueller, Managing Director of PocketBook Readers GmbH. “We are also glad to offer content, protected by LCP DRM: with this solution, we ensure greater flexibility and fewer barriers – staying true to our mission of making reading as user-friendly as possible.”

“We are delighted to be working with PocketBook to bring our Publishers’ e-books and audiobooks to new heights, giving the UK public full access to the Gardners catalog”, stated Ali Balaban, Gardners’ Head of Digital Product. “As a trusted partner in the book business, we are excited to be working with our first e-reader brand”.

Nigel Wyman, Chief Sales Officer, commented, “This is a culmination of hard work between PocketBook and the Gardners’ team. We are pleased to be able to finally offer our full catalog of digital products to a wider audience in the UK via this collaboration”.

Wrap Up

The PocketBook Era Lite offers a specific set of benefits tailored for readers who want physical buttons, premium screen tech, and freedom from closed e-book ecosystems.

Superior Text Clarity & Contrast

    • Sunken Screen Benefit: By removing the flush glass cover layer, it eliminates a layer of glare.
    • Newer Tech: It uses an E Ink Carta 1300 panel, which provides sharper text and faster page turns than the older standard Era.
    • Less Reflection: The recessed design mimics physical paper better than smooth, glossy screens.
    • Physical Buttons: Side page-turn buttons let you read comfortably with one hand without smudging the screen.
    • Auto-Rotation: A built-in G-sensor automatically flips the orientation, making it equally comfortable for left- and right-handed readers.
    • Remappable Layout: You can fully customize what the four hardware buttons do in the Linux settings.
    • No File Conversion: Natively supports 25 file formats (including EPUB, PDF, AZW, and MOBI).
    • Drag-and-Drop Friendly: You do not need to use proprietary software like Calibre or Amazon Send-to-Kindle to load your books.
    • Multiple Sync Options: Move files easily via Dropbox, Send-to-PocketBook, or a direct USB-C cable.
  • Native Libby App: Unlike Kindles outside the US, the built-in Libby app lets you browse, borrow, and download library books directly on the device over Wi-Fi.
  • Open DRM Support: Built-in Adobe and LCP DRM compatibility means you can buy books from almost any digital store worldwide.

entries.title: Inkleaf is a dual screen e-reader set for a Kickstarter Launch
entries.summary: The InkLeaf device is a dual-screen foldable E Ink notebook that connects two 10.3-inch Carta E Ink panels with a notebook-style hinge, letting users read reference material on one side and write handwritten notes on the other simultaneously. The post Inkleaf is a dual screen e-reader set for a Kickstarter Launch first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Inkleaf foldable digital notebook is a dual-screen E Ink tablet built specifically to solve the “split-screen problem” by allowing you to read a textbook on one side while taking notes on the other. The tablet is built to mimic the physical experience of a hardcover book.

The Inkleaf is a dual-screen E Ink digital notebook engineered with a premium cast aluminum body and a precision hinge barrel that allows it to fold completely flat into a 180-degree, two-page layout. The device features two 10.3-inch E Ink Carta 1300 panels designed to look and feel like an open hardcover book. Despite housing two full-sized screens, it remains remarkably portable, measuring just 4.2mm thin per individual panel (8.4mm when folded closed) and weighing a mere 480 grams.

Under the hood, the hardware runs on a quad-core Cortex-A35 processor, 2 GB RAM, and 64 GB onboard storage. It is powered by a 3,200 mAh battery that delivers up to two weeks of battery life on a single charge. It provides native, format-restriction-free support for PDF, EPUB, MOBI, and TXT files, eliminating recurring subscription fees for managing personal documents. The tablet also features integrated, on-device AI-powered handwriting search that lets users instantly locate phrases across all of their handwritten notebooks, alongside a specialized Secondary Display Mode that allows it to function as an eye-strain-free portable monitor for external devices.

The Inkleaf is going to run on Google Android, but it has not been disclosed on what version it is running or if it will include access to the Google Play Store to download millions of free apps. It would be dire if the company only allowed for the sideloading of apps, which would limit mass market appeal.

For writing and user input, the system includes physical page-navigation buttons and ships with a Wacom-supported, pressure-sensitive stylus that operates without a battery or charging requirements. The pen mimics the drag of a physical pen on paper and supports intuitive gesture controls, such as flipping the pen to erase or using shortcuts to flick open documents from one screen to the other. It will have 4096 levels of pressure sensitivity. Currently priced at approximately $450 USD, the initial founder and crowdfunding hardware batches are scheduled to ship in August 2026, with a broader commercial retail rollout planned for 2027.

entries.title: Zinwa Q27 looks like a Blackberry Bold or Classic
entries.summary: The Zinwa Q27 is a newly developed 5G Android 16 smartphone that features a built-in physical QWERTY keyboard inspired by classic BlackBerry designs The post Zinwa Q27 looks like a Blackberry Bold or Classic first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Zinwa Q27 is an upcoming, newly designed Android smartphone featuring a physical QWERTY keyboard that heavily channels the classic, nostalgic aesthetic of BlackBerry devices. Unlike the company’s previous Q25 project, which modified older BlackBerry hardware carcasses, the Q27 is a completely new device built from scratch.

The Zinwa Q27 is a unique 5G Android smartphone featuring a physical QWERTY keyboard and a 3.92-inch AMOLED screen with a resolution of 1080 x 1240 pixels. It delivers snappy performance using a MediaTek Dimensity 7300 processor paired with an impressive 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. It is powered by a 4,000 mAh non-removable battery that supports 15W wireless charging and 33W fast charging with a USB 2.0 Type-C port. Rounding out its core hardware are a 50MP rear camera, a 16MP selfie camera, and modern eSIM support. It measures 140 x 74 x 11mm (5.5″ x 2.9″ x 0.4″) and weighs 192 grams (6.8 ounces) and comes in black or white color options.

The Q27 is running on Android 16 with full access to Google Mobile Services, including Google Play, Google Books, and Google Maps. Readers will be able to download the latest versions of Kindle, Kobo, NOOK, Comixology, Zinio, and everything else.

I am a big fan of Blackberry Phones; I had the Blackberry Bold 9700 and the Blackberry Classic that ran Android, and the Q27 harkens back to the age where these phones reigned supreme for business, except it has a modern OS and powerful hardware. I will be getting one to review and likely keep.

The phone is available to pre-order for $589 for the 256 GB version or $673 for the 512GB version. It can be ordered on the Zinwa site, but it is unknown when it will ship out.

entries.title: Amazon forcing everyone to use their new Books Page
entries.summary: Manage all your books in one place. Your Books now offers more content management options for Kindle, Audible, and print books. Now you can return borrows, deliver to devices, discover new content, and more. The post Amazon forcing everyone to use their new Books Page first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Amazon books page is something many people don’t know about; it’s been around for a few years, but the company is now redirecting all customers to this new page, and it is time to explain exactly what it does, since the average user would be unfamiliar with it. Here is everything you need to know about the Books page.

Amazon is now redirecting all customers to their Books Page, which lists all of the hardcovers, paperbacks, Kindle Books, and Audible Audiobooks that have been purchased from Audible. You can filter by both print and digital in order to see everything you have purchased, and it also tells you how long you have been using your Amazon account. There is also a new AI button that scans all of your purchases and provides live recommendations.

What is very compelling about the new Books page is that you can read your Kindle Books using the Kindle Cloud Reader, which automatically opens when you click Read Now, next to a Kindle book. Audiobooks purchased from Audible also have a new Listen tab, which opens a new audiobook player that plays it, without being redirected to the Audible website. If you have a subscription to Kindle Unlimited, text appears next to the title, indicating whether you have returned it or are in the process of reading it. You can also return Kindle Unlimited books by clicking on the book and selecting Manage.

If you have multiple Kindle e-readers in the household that are attached to the same Amazon account, you can deliver the books to each of your devices by clicking on Manage, and there will be a dropdown menu listing all of the Kindle e-readers and Kindle apps. Both e-books and audiobooks can be delivered to your device in this manner.

entries.title: Free Ink is an open source project for e-reader OS
entries.summary: Free Ink is an active, open-source collective dedicated to building a completely open e-reader ecosystem that spans software, firmware, and hardware. The post Free Ink is an open source project for e-reader OS first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Free Ink is an open-source collective building the software, firmware, and hardware for e-paper readers.. Community-built, fully open-source firmware for budget e-paper readers, with more features, more control, and an open base anyone can build on. It currently supports Xteink X4, Xteink X3, de-link, LilyGo T5 S3, Sticky, and M5Paper v1.1.

Free Ink parses EPUB 2 and 3, applies embedded CSS, and lays out chapters in your font, size, and margins. Pages are cached to SD on first open, so every reopen is near-instant. Noto Serif and Noto Sans built in, plus any font loaded from your SD card. Tune size, spacing, margins, hyphenation, alignment, and anti-aliasing. The reader runs an upload server over WiFi. Drop EPUBs in from any browser, send straight from Calibre, and keep your place across devices with KOReader sync. Full right-to-left layout for Hebrew and Arabic, plus translated menus in Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Ukrainian, Polish and more.

Not only is several e-readers fully supported, but the company has a software framework on GitHub that allows developers, hackers, tinkers and brands to experiment on their own hardware.

entries.title: reTerminal Sticky is a tiny E INK, AI-powered magnetic display
entries.summary: Sticky is a 3.97-inch AI-powered magnetic ePaper display that keeps your family connected through visible notes, weather updates, and thoughtful messages. The post reTerminal Sticky is a tiny E INK, AI-powered magnetic display first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The reTerminal Sticky is an AI-powered magnetic e‑paper note device developed by Seeed Studio, designed specifically as a dedicated shared reminder screen for households. Instead of keeping reminders buried in a phone, Sticky makes important notes, to-dos, and warm family messages visible in places like the fridge, kitchen, hallway, or entryway. It is available on September 15th and retails for $49.99 on the Sticky Website.

Sticky features a crisp 3.4-inch E-Ink touchscreen with a resolution of 800 x 480. It is packed into a compact 4.5-inch outer frame. Users press an onboard physical button to speak, and the device instantly transcribes voice into notes or to-do lists. Built with an integrated magnetic backing and an extra adhesive magnetic ring for toolless mounting to refrigerators or non-metal walls. The e-paper screen lets the device run up to a week on a single charge under normal use, or months in Battery Saver Mode via the 750 mAh battery.

Use the Seeedash mobile App to manage your devices remotely and update content on the fly. Add a reminder or leave a surprise photo – all from your phone, and it shows up on the Sticky instantly for your family to see. For more creative control, use Seeedash Web to customize and deploy your content. Stay connected even when you’re miles away, however it only has a paltry 32MB of storage, but does have an SD card capable of 32GB.

People who just want to buy the device and use it normally can do so. However, it has a tremendous open source community behind it. It runs on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller with full open-source development tool chains. The community actively utilizes the device via ESPHome and custom OpenDisplay firmware to link it directly into Home Assistant. This allows developers to use the E-ink touch interface for smart home automations like room-by-room light controls. Supports flashing dedicated SenseCraft Human-Machine Interface firmware to deploy custom dashboard designs easily. It is fully compatible with CrossPoint, to turn the Sticky into an e-reader.

entries.title: What is better, the Kindle Scribe 2024 or the Kindle Scribe 2025?
entries.summary: The 3rd Generation Amazon Kindle Scribe features an expanded 11-inch E Ink Oxide display, a thinner 5.4 mm profile, a lighter 400g build, and a faster quad-core processor with 12ms writing latency. In contrast, the 2nd Generation Scribe uses a 10.2-inch screen, a thicker asymmetrical bezel layout, and an older processor stack. The post What is better, the Kindle Scribe 2024 or the Kindle Scribe 20
entries.content:
The 2025 Kindle Scribe (3rd Generation) introduces a completely redesigned exterior, a larger display, and faster processing capabilities compared to the 2024 model. The 2025 version supports cloud storage providers such as Microsoft OneDrive and Google Drive, and it also includes several new AI features.

Kindle Scribe 2025 and 2026

  • Performance & Writing: The 2025 model runs on a snappier processor, creating a faster user interface and noticeably lower writing latency
  • Screen Clarity vs. Texture: The 2025 monochrome screen offers a whiter background and crisper text clarity. However, some users note this smoother screen layer slightly reduces the gritty, paper-like friction felt when writing on the 2024 version.
  • Smarter Software: The 2025 model includes new AI-powered tools that make searching notes smarter and more intuitive. This lets you type searches to instantly pull up handwritten notes.
  • Universal Note Search: Enter loose keywords into the main top search bar to index your cursive and print handwriting. The Kindle locates matching terms globally across your stored notebooks and identifies exact page numbers
  • Send to Alexa: is a feature that works with the user’s notes written on the Kindle Scribe and Scribe Colorsoft. Users can submit their notebooks or documents to the AI, which will then help with brainstorming new ideas, guidance for projects, or turning your notes into to-do lists.
  • Color Variant: Amazon expanded the 2025 lineup to include the premium Kindle Scribe Colorsoft for users wanting color highlights and document viewing.
  • Ask Notebooks: is a built-in generative AI search feature on the Kindle Scribe. It lets you search handwritten text, uncover insights, and ask conversational follow-up questions directly about your notebooks.
  • AI Reading Tools: Access upcoming reading companions like “Story So Far” for spoiler-free series catch-ups and “Ask This Book” to clear up narrative confusion as you read.
  • Larger Screen, Smaller Body: The screen footprint is increased from 10.2 inches to 11 inches while shrinking the bezels. This configuration gives you more writing space without expanding the tablet’s physical size.

Kindle Scribe 2024

The 2024 Kindle Scribe refresh introduces several hardware refinements, distinct visual styling, and the debut of built-in generative AI tools. It serves as a middle-ground upgrade focusing on a premium tactile feel and focused productivity.

  • Uniform White Borders: The device ditches asymmetric bezels for a clean, flush-front display surrounded by uniform white borders.
  • Paper-Like Screen Micro-Texture: The 300 PPI glare-free screen features an altered surface coating. This design gives the pen tip extra “bite” and friction to closely mimic real paper.
  • Upgraded Premium Pen: The standard bundle includes a re-weighted Premium Pen. It features a customizable shortcut button and a soft-tipped eraser that behaves like a traditional pencil.
  • Premium Color Options: The aluminum chassis comes in Metallic Jade and Tungsten finishes.
  • AI Note Summarization: Long, handwritten brainstorms or meeting minutes can be compressed into a bulleted summary directly on the device.
  • Active Canvas: When writing in a standard Kindle book, your stylus strokes dynamically move the layout. The software side panels expand automatically to fit your notes without burying the underlying text.

Wrap Up

The Kindle Scribe 3rd generation, Kindle Scribe Colorsoft, and Kindle Scribe without Front-Light are all models that have a ton of AI features, but tend to run on the more expensive side. The screen quality is better and larger than the 2024 model, and the screen has better resistance to drawing with the pen.

The Kindle Scribe 2024 model is good enough for most people and perfect for those who don’t use AI enhancements. This iteration of the Scribe is good enough for people who want to freehand draw, read Kindle books on a very large screen, and draw inside of them too. This is likely the most affordable Kindle Scribe, which also regularly goes on sale.

Like-New Amazon Kindle Scribe (16GB) - Your notes, documents and books, all in one place. With...

  • Like-New Amazon Kindle Scribe 16GB is refurbished, tested, and certified to look and work like new and comes with the same limited warranty as a new device. Like-New Amazon devices may be packaged in generic Amazon-branded boxes.
  • Kindle Scribe - A Kindle and a notebook, all in one. Redesigned flush-front display with uniform white borders and upgraded Premium Pen, feels like writing on paper.
  • Write in books – Start writing on the page and Active Canvas will create space for your notes. Expand the margins to add more notes, or collapse them to see the original page.

Amazon Kindle Scribe (16GB) - Your notes, documents and books, all in one place. With built-in AI...

  • A digital notebook for all your writing needs - Replace your stack of notebooks with a single device purpose-built for writing, reading, and thinking. No notifications or social media.
  • With AI tools to transform your notes - Convert messy handwriting into readable font, summarize your notes, and change their length and tone with built-in AI notebook tools.
  • Feels like pen on paper - See, feel and hear your thoughts meet the page with every stroke of the Premium Pen. No need to set up or charge, just start writing.

entries.title: Instapaper 10 brings tons of new features to iOS
entries.summary: Instapaper 10 is the biggest update to the iOS application in over a decade, introducing a comprehensive design overhaul alongside major feature updates. The post Instapaper 10 brings tons of new features to iOS first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Instapaper 10 is the biggest update to the iOS application in over a decade, introducing a comprehensive design overhaul alongside major feature updates. Released in late July 2026, the milestone release modernizes the save-for-later reading environment and accompanies a fully rebuilt web platform and new Android capabilities. “Instapaper 10 is our biggest update to the iOS app in over a decade. It’s a large redesign that adopts Liquid Glass, along with several new features and performance improvements.

Instapaper 10 is our biggest update to the iOS app in over a decade. It’s a large redesign that adopts Liquid Glass, along with several new features and performance improvements.

Section Counts: All sections now display a count of the articles or notes they contain. If section counts feel more anxiety-inducing than helpful, you can turn them off in Settings > Behavior > Section Counts.



Section Sorting: To sort your Folders or Tags, tap the “…” menu next to the section header and choose your preferred sort option.



Article List Appearance: They introduced Condensed View, new typography and styles, and an easy way to adjust the article list’s appearance. From an article list, tap “…”, then tap “Appearance” to adjust styles, fonts, and image thumbnails.

New Reading Fonts: They are introducing four new reading fonts in this release, two serifs and two sans-serifs: Literata, New York, Open Sans, and Atkinson Hyperlegible.

Home Screen Widget: Last but not least, we’re excited to launch a Home Screen widget for iOS. It displays your in-progress article and your most recently saved articles, and provides a one-tap shortcut to start reading your Instapaper saves.

They improved iPad multitasking, redesigned onboarding, made background syncing more reliable, and reduced article download times in this release. Together, these changes make this the fastest and best version of Instapaper for iOS yet.

Platform-Wide Ecosystem Improvements: Rebuilt Website: Accompanied by the mobile launch, the web version of Instapaper received its second-ever full platform rebuild since its original launch in 2008.

Android AI Voices: The Android app rebuilt its text-to-speech architecture from scratch to officially integrate premium, natural AI narration.

entries.title: Dasung Link 2 Review – A Smartphone Monitor
entries.summary: The Dasung Link 2 is a specialized 6.7-inch portable E-Ink smartphone monitor designed to reduce eye strain by mirroring your phone’s display onto a paper-like, glare-free surface. The post Dasung Link 2 Review – A Smartphone Monitor first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Dasung Link 2 is a specialized 6.7-inch portable E-Ink smartphone monitor designed to reduce eye strain by mirroring your phone’s display onto a paper-like, glare-free surface. It is not a standalone phone; it lacks its own processor, cellular radio, and operating system, meaning it completely relies on your connected smartphone’s hardware and apps to function.

The Dasung Link 2 features a 6.7-inch monochrome E-Ink display with a pixel density of 300 PPI. This crisp resolution mimics the reading quality of premium e-readers, ensuring text is incredibly sharp and easy on the eyes. It utilizes ambient light reflection and includes an adjustable dual-tone front light for comfortable night reading.

The Link 2 is equipped with DASUNG’s signature high-speed refresh technology operating at 60Hz, enabling fluid scrolling, typing, and video playback that closely mimic those of a standard LCD screen, with minimal ghosting. It uses wireless screen mirroring to broadcast displays seamlessly from both iOS and Android devices. Enables you to control your smartphone directly by tapping and swiping on the E-Ink screen itself.

The device is built with an ultra-thin, lightweight metal body featuring multi-function physical keys for easy image enhancement and contrast adjustments. It is also compatible with magnetic power banks for convenient outdoor use. The monitor does not contain an internal battery to keep it lightweight. Instead, it features dual USB-C ports and is typically powered by an external source.

It is important to note that the Link 2 inherits your phone’s CPU, RAM, and app performance to work properly. It is compatible with Android 12 and later, as well as modern versions of iOS and HarmonyOS. It retails for $329 from the Dasung website for the battery-free version or $349 for the battery variant. Space Grey and Glacier Blue are the two available colors.
